subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic delayed/batch agent-turn lifecycle across provider runtime, Plugin SDK, gateway protocol, and background execution surfaces, or intentionally defer provider Batch API support?
rationale: The request crosses public API, provider auth eligibility, model routing, session/transcript state, delivery timing, fallback behavior, accounting, and config/protocol surfaces, so automation cannot choose the permanent contract safely.

options.title: Design generic delayed turns
options.body: Add the provider-neutral lifecycle first, then implement OpenAI and Anthropic Batch API support through that seam for cron, sessions, subagents, and heartbeat.

options.title: Limit to a cron shortcut
options.body: Implement a narrower cron/provider flag faster, accepting higher migration and behavior-drift risk across other background surfaces.

options.title: Defer Batch API support
options.body: Keep current real-time execution as the supported behavior and document why provider Batch APIs are out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Design generic delayed turns
recommendation.body: Add the provider-neutral lifecycle first, then implement OpenAI and Anthropic Batch API support through that seam for cron, sessions, subagents, and heartbeat.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across the provider runtime and isolated cron execution boundaries that need the first design decision.
